##: Point Hub for Windows through Scoop, without a bucket: scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lucanepa/openvolley/main/escoresheet/packaging/scoop/point-hub.json

Point Hub is KSC Wiedikon's scoreboard console (github.com/Lucanepa/point-hub). This runs its official .msi silently (the same one winget and the download page use), so the app is installed per machine to Program Files with its Start menu entry.

Regenerate for a new version: escoresheet/packaging/scoop/update-manifests.sh point-hub VERSION. Until the first release the hash is the @SHA256@ placeholder, which Scoop refuses. README.md next to this file says more.
description: Point Hub: the console of the KSCW LedBox scoreboard, for the scorer's table.
notes: Point Hub was installed with its own installer (one administrator prompt) to Program Files, like a download from the website. Start it from the Start menu.
It does not update itself: 'scoop update point-hub' installs each new version over the old one.

script: # Downloaded as point-hub.msi_: under its own name Scoop would unpack the .msi instead of running it
Write-Host 'Running the Point Hub installer (Windows asks for administrator rights)...'
if ($p.ExitCode -ne 0 -and $p.ExitCode -ne 3010) { abort "The Point Hub installer stopped (exit code $($p.ExitCode))." }
# 'scoop update': the new .msi upgrades this version in place (same UpgradeCode), so no uninstall first
# Point Hub's UpgradeCode, fixed for good in point-hub's android/desktop/build.gradle.kts
if (!$codes) { warn 'Point Hub is not installed any more (removed in Settings > Apps?): nothing to uninstall.'; return }
# silent: the settings and backups (%APPDATA%\Point Hub, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Point Hub) stay
if (@((New-Object -ComObject WindowsInstaller.Installer).RelatedProducts($upgrade))) { warn 'Point Hub is still installed: uninstall it in Settings > Apps.' }
